items.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: Shotgun Kelly was a cop in Johnstown, Pennsylvania, and he was a drummer, a show drummer. He taught me how to play drums.

ctx.x: Yeah. And Shotgun Kelly a man that came to be known, Shotgun Kelly was a cop in Johnstown, Pennsylvania, and he was a drummer, a show drummer. He taught me how to play drums. I do drums also by the way. I’ve taught many drummers how to be a show drummer. Play between my legs, behind my back, spin the sticks, just like Lionel does. I learned that from Shotgun Kelly before I met Lionel — no right after I met Lionel. And Shotgun knew how to get onstage and do a dissertation. He could speak, at random, at

any audience. This is when it was hard for blacks to do, ’58, ’59. Blacks are in now. Back then to be outstanding, you better be good, if you’re dark-skinned. You better give the white people a reason to want to sit there and watch you. Otherwise why should they? So I can thank God for having the best training school in the world. And I never studied formally except for one semester. Yet I studied Haydn’s “Trumpet Concerto,” I know the “Trumpeter’s Holiday,” and “Flight of the Bumblebee.” I took it upon myself to…
